newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Proton sees strong net profit for FY96/97.
newsitem.headline: Proton sees strong net profit for FY96/97.

text.p: Malaysia's Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton) said on Thursday that it expects strong net profit growth for the current financial year ending March 31, 1997 due to higher car sales volume.

"Given that the volume we are forecasting this financial year is stronger than last year, given that all the assumptions are correct...it should be strong," said Proton director Tengku Mahaleel Tengku Ariff. He declined to give further details.
He told a press conference after the company's annual meeting that the national car maker is predicting unit sales of 180,000 of which 20 percent will be exported.

Proton posted a net profit of 355.88 million ringgit on turnover of 5.17 billion ringgit for the year ended March 31, 1996, up from 232.12 million and 3.71 billion ringgit respectively in the previous year.

Tengku Mahaleel said Proton has introduced a no-frills car from August 31 through its distributor, Edaran Otomobil Nasional Bhd. The no-frills Proton Iswara 1.3 litre model is priced at 35,320 ringgit.

Tengku Mahaleel said the no-frills Iswara has different internal fittings and mechnical components from the present model. He said Proton wants to get feedback from potential buyers before deciding on full production.
Proton also plans to export its 2.0 litre Proton Perdana model to neighbouring countries within a year, he said.
